lines.text: In nineteen eighty-four, an ice cream driver cracked a TV game show â€”
and won a hundred ten thousand dollars without cheating once.
See, Press Your Luck flashed an eighteen-square light board.
Contestants slammed buzzers avoiding cartoon Whammies that wiped them out.
Everyone thought the lights bounced randomly.
Except Michael Larson paused home tapes frame by frame,
and noticed the computer only looped five fixed patterns.
Even better, squares four and eight had zero Whammies â€”
and always paid cash plus an extra spin.
Michael memorized the rhythm until his timing locked in.
On live TV, he hit spin after spin â€” forty-five straight turns â€”
while network bosses panicked and yelled cut the cameras.
Lawyers searched the rulebook, found zero rules broken,
and had to pay him every single penny.
CBS quietly reprogrammed the board the very next week.
